scene.title: Why Methane Is Tetrahedral
scene.summary: Carbon’s four bonding pairs repel equally, giving a tetrahedral shape with 109.5° H‑C‑H angles.

beats.title: Methane molecule
beats.narration: Here is a methane molecule: a carbon atom bonded to four hydrogens.

beats.title: VSEPR predicts tetrahedral
beats.narration: Carbon has four bonding pairs, so VSEPR predicts a tetrahedral arrangement.

check.question: What is the H–C–H bond angle in a perfect tetrahedron?
check.explain: A tetrahedron gives 109.5° between any two bonds.

beats.title: Show the angle
beats.narration: The H–C–H angle is 109.5°, matching the tetrahedral geometry.

beats.title: Recap
beats.narration: Methane is tetrahedral because four electron pairs repel equally, producing 109.5° bond angles.
